name: Copyable Result
summary: A copyable result is what an action produced — a built URL, a key, a receipt — with a button to copy it. Use it wherever a value is generated rather than typed. It is made almost entirely of other components, each of which can announce on its own, so the work is deciding that only the panel speaks.
demoNote: Everything under Common mistakes is live and measured. Example 2 prints how narrow the same URL is willing to be under three wrapping rules, and two of the three look identical on screen.

contract.useWhen: A computed value, with exactly one thing inside it that talks.
states: empty — aria-disabled=true on the copy button, not the disabled attribute, so it keeps its tab stop and can explain itself
keyboard: the copy button is a stop; the value is a code element, not a control
native: copies from the focused button, and announces the outcome
failureModes: an output element for the value — it has an implicit role=status and reads the whole value on every change
four live regions in one panel, each defensible on its own
the copy button renamed to a past tense, so the control under your finger changes
a tick as the only confirmation, correctly aria-hidden and therefore silent
overflow-wrap:break-word for a long token, which wraps the text and leaves min-content alone (SC 1.4.10)
a refusal announced in the region — nothing changed, so put the reason on the button
